title: microburst prefill deferral and kernel probing for tail reduction
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: Summary: Continuous batching currently experiences microburst-driven tail latency from two correlated causes: (1) brief high-concurrency spikes cause large, heterogeneous batches that force worst-case kernel paths and increase kv-cache pressure; (2) lack of proactive kernel selection per-batch means some batches use decode kernels optimized for large batch throughput but suffer on sub-batch microbursts. Proposed solution combines a lightweight microburst detector + short prefills deferral admission gate, a per-batch kernel-probing step (cheap hardware-aware microbenchmark) to pick small-batch vs throughput kernel variants, and a decode scheduling policy that opportunistically reorders or defers low-priority prefill work to reduce stragglers.
goals: Reduce system-wide p99 decode latency for mixed workloads by 30%-60% under microburst scenarios; limit median increase to <5% and avoid throughput loss >3%. Provide telemetry and rollback knobs. Ensure backwards-compatible API and tenant isolation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Benchmarked synthetic microburst scenario shows p99 drop >= 30% vs baseline (same model/hardware). 2) No more than 3% throughput regression in 95% of steady-state traces. 3) Feature has feature flag and runtime knobs for hold-duration, probe sample-size, and priority classification. 4) Automated integration e2e test that replays production trace and asserts SLOs in CI.
approach: 1) Microburst detector: sliding-window token-admission counter per-queue + exponential backoff hold (default hold 8-20ms, tenant-weighted). 2) Prefill deferral: short, probabilistic delay on certain prefill requests (configurable per-route) to allow microburst coalescing into more kernel-friendly shapes; low-priority requests get longer defer. 3) Kernel probing: on first N batches per-node per-minute probe cheap single-run throughput/latency for alternate kernel variants (int4 vs int8/attention-optimized kernels) and tag upcoming batches; probes are low-overhead and use reserved short probe slots. 4) Decode scheduler: assign decode slots according to predicted kernel affinity and request priority; gracefully preempt/evict decode slots that exceed predicted tail risk. 5) Observability: add metrics for hold events, probe outcomes, kernel-choice histogram, per-tenant p99, and a pump for tracebacks to tie kernel selection to tail events.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Risk: excessive deferral could increase median latency if mis-configured. Mitigation: conservative default hold and per-route opt-out.
- Risk: probe overhead interfering with tight SLOs. Mitigation: cap probe rate and run on isolated probe slots per GPU.
- Tradeoff: kernel specialization reduces worst-case p99 but may fragment cache/occupancy and slightly lower peak throughput; plan to measure and provide a global knob to prefer throughput vs tail.
- Operational risk: additional metrics increase cardinality; we'll roll metrics behind a sampling flag.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): implement microburst detector + simple probabilistic deferral; unit tests and basic metrics. Phase 2 (3 wks): add kernel-probe module and integrate kernel-choice tag into admission pipeline; offline simulation and cluster dogfood. Phase 3 (2 wks): decode scheduler priority integration, e2e CI replay tests, dashboards and rollout plan. Phase 4 (1 wk): staged rollout behind feature flag + canary on 5% traffic then 25%/50%/100% with automated rollback criteria.
